title.narrative: Urban Water Supply and Sanitation Sector Project

description.narrative: The project will implement high priority components following the government's water and sanitation sector plan to increase access to piped water supply and sanitation service, especially among the poor households; reduce reliance on groundwater and rainwater harvest and ensure more efficient use of water. The project will also enhance hygiene awareness, promote water conservation and improve fecal sludge management.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Efficiency, accessibility, climate change and disaster resiliency, and sustainability of safe water and sanitation improved in the GHA, and the towns of Auki, Gizo, Munda, Noro, and Tulagi

14,000 households (64%) in GHA access improved on-site sanitation policies and fecal sludge management. (2019 baseline: 0 households) (OP 3.3.2) Progress/Status: Progress towards achieving the target of 14,000 households in greater Honiara benefiting from improved onsite sanitation policies is on track following the preparation of the draft greater Honiara Area Comprehensive Sanitation Plan 2022 - 2026. The draft Plan now requires ratification by Honiara City Council and Guadalcanal Province before the finalization of septage treatment plant design (design scheduled to be completed by Q3 2026). Data Source: Honiara City Council Environmental Health Unit reports Actual value:

SIWA continues to recover its annual O&M costs, asset depreciation costs, and debt servicing costs from user charges and government community service obligation payments (2019 baseline: 100%) (OP 4.1.1) Progress/Status: Full recovery of annual operation and maintenance costs, asset depreciation costs, and debt servicing costs from user charges and government community service obligation payments is essential for SW's financial sustainability. SW achieved full cost recovery in 2020, 2022, 2023, and 2024, and narrowly missed the target in 2021 (by less than 3%). SIWA is implementing further measures to strengthen the financial sustainability of SW including annual cost of service and tariff reviews, and equally important, further investments to reduce nonrevenue water. Data Source: SIWA annual report; and SIWA annual audit reports Actual value:

2,000 households in GHA are connected to a sewer network. (2019 baseline: 600 households) (OP 4.1) Achievement: 692 Progress/Status: At end December 2025, 692 households were connected to the SW's sewerage networks. placing the project target of 4,000 connections at risk. Ongoing trunk sewerage works and the proposed eastern outfall subproject are expected to address persistent coastal water quality issues in East Honiara once implemented. Data Source: SIWA annual report; and Pacific Water Utility Benching Report, Pacific Water and Wastewater Association, published annually

Nonrevenue water in GHA is reduced to 30% (2019 baseline: 62%) (OP 4.2.2) Achievement: 60.8 Progress/Status: NRW across all SIWA water supply networks averaged 60.8% in 2025. Overall, the project is off-track to reach the project NRW target in Honiara of 30% or less by 2027. Lack of progress on NRW is driven by primarily by aging infrastructure and high commercial losses. Substantial investments are required to reduce NRW including expediting water main renewals. Bids for the replacement of 12km of trunk water mains in Honiara with high leakage is ongoing. Investigations in 2022 indicate that about 64km of water mains in Honiara suffer substantial leakage and require full replacement. Further investments, including replacement of water meters and customer connections to reduce commercial and physical losses is also planned. Data Source: SIWA annual report; and Pacific Water Utility Benching Report, Pacific Water and Wastewater Association, published annually

By July 2028: 16,500 households, including 12% households headed by women, use improved and climate- and disaster-resilient water supplies. (2019 baseline: 9,000) (OP 2.4.1, OP 3.2.5, OP 4.1) Achievement: 17653 Progress/Status: SW has surpassed the project's water supply coverage target of 16,500 households with 17,653 households connected at the end of December 2025. Data Source: SIWA annual report; and SIWA water production records released monthly

Sewage discharged from the sewer system complies with water quality standards in GHA. (2019 baseline: 0%) (OP 3.3.4) Progress/Status: The water quality compliance target for sewage discharged from the Honiara sewer systems remains dependent on timely reconfiguration of the Honiara sewer system. Preparation of bidding documents for the eastern outfall subproject is ongoing. Due to insufficient funding to construct both planned new outfalls, the eastern outfall—handling the majority of sewage flows—has been prioritized. This prioritization increases the likelihood of meeting water quality compliance thresholds, but overall progress remains delayed pending procurement and financing decisions. Data Source: SIWA annual report; and Pacific Water Utility Benching Report, Pacific Water and Wastewater Association, published annually Base year: 2019 Baseline value: N/A
